ageRange: 12-25 (must not have turned 26 on the departure date)
appliesTo: SAS Young on SAS-operated flights, Economy only (marketed as SAS Go). SAS and 2026 trade coverage describe it as covering Scandinavian and wider European routes plus long-haul. A SAS youth-tickets page says youth tickets are for round trips, in a sentence tied to destinations outside Europe; SAS does not clearly say whether one-way tickets are sold within Europe (a 2022 third-party blog quoted single-flight youth fares on Copenhagen-Hamburg).
benefit: Lower price than the regular fare (SAS wording: minimum 10% on all SAS flights, up to 70% on less popular departures); change date/time as often as wanted until departure, only the fare difference is payable (SAS Young FAQ); EuroBonus points earned as on a normal ticket. SAS Young Standard includes one 23 kg checked bag; SAS Young Light on flights within Europe has only a small underseat bag. Both are non-refundable.
typicalSaving: SAS states at least 10% and up to 70%. Third-party example (travel-dealz, 9 May 2026): Copenhagen-Berlin 13-14 June, cheapest regular fare EUR 251, about 31% saving on the morning/evening flight; Copenhagen-New York return from about EUR 515 vs about EUR 591 regular (no checked bag).
howToBook: flysas.com or the SAS app: start from the SAS Young page and select the Youth/Young (12-25 years) passenger category for each young traveller. Youth and adult passengers cannot share one reservation (book separately, or book everyone as adults). A third-party article says the fares sit in booking classes V and O.
conditions: Valid physical ID shown at the airport to prove age 12-25 (passport, national ID card or driving licence; digital IDs not accepted; SAS FAQ says a driving licence is only accepted within and between Sweden, Norway and Denmark, so carry passport or national ID card for Europe). Boarding can be refused and the trip cancelled if age cannot be proven. Cannot be combined with the Unaccompanied Minor service. Limited availability, not every flight or date has a Young fare.
relevantForTRD: Yes, the most directly useful option: SAS flies from Trondheim (Oslo, Copenhagen, Stockholm and others) so a TRD-hub-Europe trip on SAS-operated flights can be booked on Young fares with no student proof.
notes: flysas.com blocks direct fetches (403 / bot check), so SAS page content was read through search-engine extracts restricted to flysas.com; the extracts agree across several SAS pages. The last three sources are third-party (trade news, travel-dealz May 2026, a 2022 blog) and were used only for examples. Conflicts: the Young FAQ says date/time changes are free (fare difference only) while the general SAS rebooking page lists a fee from 650 NOK/SEK/DKK; SAS introduced new ticket types on 1 Oct 2025 so Light/Standard contents may have changed; round-trip-only wording is ambiguous. Not checked: live Young prices on TRD routes.

ageRange: 12-25 (cannot be 26 or older on the departure date)
appliesTo: Selected routes in Norwegian's network, subject to availability. The booking page describes the youth price on routes in Norway and within the Nordic countries and the US-site page text describes it as covering flights within Europe; no authoritative route list was found, so eligibility of a given European route has to be checked in the booking flow. Fare types covered are not stated.
benefit: Lower price on eligible routes (no percentage stated); rebooking without a change fee, only the fare difference (stated for bookings from 26 Feb 2025).
howToBook: norwegian.com: choose the Youth ticket type for the passenger, or enter promo code UNDER26.
conditions: Valid photo ID at check-in or boarding (passport, national ID card or driving licence); without it boarding can be refused with no refund, and passengers who do not meet the conditions or misuse the youth ticket can be charged a fee. Child discount does not apply to youth bookings; unaccompanied minors cannot use youth tickets; campaign prices exclude child and youth discounts. Limited seats.
relevantForTRD: Yes: Norwegian operates from Trondheim (Oslo, Bergen and some European routes per the Wikipedia airport list, possibly outdated), so TRD-Oslo and onward Norwegian flights are candidates for the Youth/UNDER26 fare, but each European route must be checked at booking.
notes: norwegian.com blocks direct fetches (403), so the text was read through search extracts restricted to norwegian.com; age rule, UNDER26 code and ID rule are consistent across language versions. Sources disagree or are silent on route scope (Norway/Nordic vs Europe) and on the discount size. Some Norwegian pages are old; one page version shows USD route prices only. Flyla's Norwegian deals page says student or youth fares exist on selected routes for verified users but states no terms.

ageRange: Youth ticket 12-25 (under 26 on the departure date). The separate Student ticket is for full-time students aged 26-31, so a 23-year-old uses the Youth ticket.
appliesTo: Widerøe-operated flights (mainly domestic regional Norway plus its few international routes), leisure travel only, limited number of youth seats per departure. No route list for Europe was found.
benefit: Youth Smart and Youth Mini fares at a lower price (no percentage stated). Youth Smart includes one 23 kg checked bag, Youth Mini only a small bag. Changes are free for tickets bought from 18 March 2026 (fare difference only). The Widerøe page says youth tickets can be combined with SAS youth and Norwegian youth fares.
howToBook: wideroe.no: choose passenger type Youth and enter the date of birth; youth and adult passengers cannot be in the same booking and the passenger type cannot be changed after booking.
conditions: Photo ID with date of birth at boarding (passengers 18+ without valid ID can be refused); false age information can mean refused check-in or boarding without refund; refundable only within 24 hours of purchase on wideroe.no; if a return has one leg on a normal Smart or Mini ticket the normal change fee applies to the whole trip.
relevantForTRD: Marginal: Widerøe is a regional carrier whose Youth fare only helps if the trip needs a domestic Norwegian leg to or from Trondheim, not for reaching Europe.
notes: wideroe.no and help.wideroe.no blocked direct fetches (403); content read through search extracts restricted to those domains. The pages describe the student ticket as 'under 32' in one place and '26-31' in another (same cutoff). The ticket-types page is old (fees there predate the 2026 free-change rule). Widerøe is reported to be dropping some Bergen international routes, so its Europe network is small.

ageRange: Youth 12-24; Student 18-29 (full-time student at an educational institution)
appliesTo: KLM Youth & Student fares, Economy only, on European and intercontinental flights. Minimum stay: at least 7 days on intercontinental flights; on European flights at least 3 days or including a Saturday/weekend. Not available on all flights and destinations.
benefit: Flexible changes (KLM Norway: tickets can be changed without extra fee, only the fare difference) and extra checked baggage: the KLM page says one extra 23 kg item on top of the standard fare allowance, while a May 2026 article on the Air France/KLM update reports two checked bags included. No discount percentage stated.
howToBook: klm.no or klm.com: choose Youth or Student as the passenger type at the start of the search, and the youth/student price is then shown automatically. A 23-year-old can use Youth (age only) or Student.
conditions: Economy only; carry passport and, for the Student variant, a student ID, student card or enrolment letter in English (checked at check-in or boarding); minimum-stay rules above; availability varies. The sister Air France page lists cancellation fees of EUR 250 (international) and EUR 100 (within Europe).
relevantForTRD: Yes: KLM flies Trondheim-Amsterdam and onward, and an 8-day trip (7-15 Dec) satisfies the 3-days-or-weekend rule for European flights, so a KLM Youth fare is worth pricing against SAS Young.
notes: klm.no timed out on direct fetch, so KLM page content was read through search extracts restricted to klm domains (Norway, US, Bonaire, Serbia, India versions agree on ages and minimum stay). KLM's kids page confirms travellers 12+ otherwise pay the regular price. Conflicts: the extra-baggage wording (one extra 23 kg bag on KLM vs two bags on the Air France page and in the May 2026 Luftfahrtmagazin article, a third-party source); older third-party pages (Dec 2024) said 21-day minimum stay and long-haul only. Not verified: that a Youth fare is actually offered on Trondheim-Amsterdam on the travel dates (needs a live search with passenger type Youth).

ageRange: Youth 12-24; Student 18-29 enrolled at an educational institution (an older Air France FAQ says a student is up to 26 and one page intro says 25-29, so the sources conflict)
appliesTo: Air France Youth and Student fares, Economy only, short-, medium- and long-haul flights marketed by Air France or KLM. Minimum stay 7 days on intercontinental flights and 3 days or a weekend on European flights. Departures from the USA, Canada and Mexico are excluded.
benefit: Up to 2 free checked bags of 23 kg; ticket changes at no cost (fare difference only); no percentage discount stated. The separate paid Youth Pass (EUR 49, up to 30% on standard fares) applies to departures from France only.
howToBook: airfrance.no or airfrance.fr: select Youth or Student in the Passengers drop-down when searching.
conditions: At check-in or the gate show valid ID plus, for students, a student card, university acceptance letter or proof of enrolment; cancellation fee EUR 250 for international and EUR 100 for flights within Europe; Economy only; subject to availability.
relevantForTRD: Possibly: it only applies to itineraries sold by Air France/KLM (for example Trondheim-Amsterdam or via Paris), so it is the same product family as the KLM Youth fare and should be priced together with it.
notes: Air France pages timed out on direct fetch; content read through search extracts restricted to airfrance domains, plus the Luftfahrtmagazin article of 17 May 2026 (third party) which reports two checked bags and free rebooking effective immediately. Older third-party guide (travel-dealz, Dec 2024, marked expired) described a 21-day minimum stay, long-haul only, and a EUR 200 rebooking fee; the current official pages supersede it. The Youth Pass list names Norway among medium-haul destinations but only for bookings from France.

ageRange: Student fare: 16 or older at verification, no upper age limit (no separate youth 12-25 fare found)
appliesTo: Lufthansa Group student fares (Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian, Brussels Airlines) on selected flights, Economy only, one-way and return, only for bookings departing from the listed origin countries and only when every flight is operated by a Lufthansa Group airline. NOT offered within Europe (the page's own example is Frankfurt to Paris); the 6 Oct 2025 press release describes intercontinental tickets and excludes Japan, Canada and the USA. Whether Norway is on the origin list could not be confirmed; Lufthansa route pages such as Trondheim-Frankfurt carry a generic 'you may be eligible for a discounted fare' sentence that contradicts the intra-Europe exclusion and looks like boilerplate.
benefit: Reduced fare (no percentage stated; the fare may not be the cheapest option), usually 2 x 23 kg free checked bags (1 x 23 kg from the USA), more flexible rebooking and refund terms than most regular fares.
howToBook: Create a Travel ID, verify student status in the Profile section (SheerID, proof of enrolment, valid one year), then search from the student fares page; eligible fares carry a Student icon. Web only, not the app. The Student fare must be booked or the free extra bag cannot be added later.
conditions: One student per booking; verification valid 1 year; student verification problems go to generationfly@dlh.de; cancellation fee may apply.
relevantForTRD: No for a Europe-only trip, because intra-European itineraries are excluded; it only matters if the group adds a long-haul leg.
notes: lufthansa.com blocks direct fetches (403); the Lufthansa Group press release (newsroom.lufthansagroup.com) was fetched directly, the student-fare pages were read through search extracts. The origin-country list on the student page was not visible in any extract. No Lufthansa youth (12-25) fare turned up in English or German searches; Lufthansa pages only describe child fares (2-11) and an unaccompanied-minor service.

ageRange: Student fare: 16 or older at verification, no upper age limit (no separate youth 12-25 fare found)
appliesTo: Same Lufthansa Group student-fare programme: selected origins only, whole itinerary on Lufthansa Group airlines, Economy only, one-way and return, and not offered for bookings within Europe.
benefit: Reduced fare (no percentage stated), usually 2 x 23 kg free checked bags, more flexible rebooking and refund terms.
howToBook: Travel ID plus student verification (SheerID) in the profile, then book Student-icon fares from the SWISS student fares page; web only.
conditions: One student per booking; the Student fare must be booked or the free bag cannot be added later; price depends on demand and may not be the lowest.
relevantForTRD: No for a Europe-only trip, since student fares are not sold for bookings within Europe.
notes: swiss.com blocks direct fetches (403); read through search extracts. SWISS child fares (2-11) are reduced but ages 12+ pay adult fares; no SWISS youth fare found. The origin list could not be seen.

ageRange: Student fare: 16 or older at verification, no upper age limit (no separate youth 12-25 fare found)
appliesTo: Same Lufthansa Group student-fare programme: selected origins only, whole itinerary on Lufthansa Group airlines, Economy only, and not offered for bookings within Europe (page example: Frankfurt to Paris).
benefit: Reduced fare (no percentage stated), usually 2 x 23 kg free checked bags (1 x 23 kg on USA-origin routes), more flexible rebooking/refund than most regular fares; a cancellation fee may apply.
howToBook: Travel ID plus student verification in the profile, then book Student-icon fares from the Austrian student fares page; when rebooking keep the student fare option to keep the extra baggage.
conditions: One student per booking; no group discounts; price based on demand and availability.
relevantForTRD: No for a Europe-only trip, since student fares are not sold for bookings within Europe.
notes: austrian.com blocks direct fetches (403); read through search extracts. Austrian booking pages show a passenger category 'Young Adults (12-15 years)' but no discount is documented for it. No Austrian youth 12-25 fare found.

ageRange: Student fare: 16 or older at verification, no upper age limit (no separate youth 12-25 fare found)
appliesTo: Same Lufthansa Group student-fare programme: selected origins only, whole itinerary on Lufthansa Group airlines, Economy only, and not offered for bookings within Europe.
benefit: Reduced fare (no percentage stated), 1 or 2 free checked bags of 23 kg depending on the route, more flexible rebooking/refund.
howToBook: Travel ID plus student verification in the profile (a private email may be used; an offer letter or student ID may be requested), then book Student-icon fares from the Brussels Airlines student fares page.
conditions: One student per booking; verification valid 1 year; the Student fare must be booked to get the free bag.
relevantForTRD: No for a Europe-only trip, since student fares are not sold for bookings within Europe.
notes: brusselsairlines.com blocks direct fetches (403); read through search extracts. Route pages list a passenger category 'Young Adults (12-15 years)' with no documented discount. A final targeted search for a Brussels youth fare could not be run because the search budget was exhausted; two earlier searches found none.

appliesTo: Eurowings student deals sold only through the Flyla platform, on selected German domestic and European Eurowings routes that are marked 'student deal'; always booked in the BASIC fare (flight plus one hand-luggage item).
benefit: Cheaper seats for verified students. Eurowings pages claim students save up to 50% (FAQ) and up to 80% (another page) on selected domestic and European flights; extra bags and seat selection cost extra.
typicalSaving: Eurowings says 'up to 50%' on one page and 'up to 80%' on another; no typical value stated.
howToBook: Register on flyla.com, verify student status (upload an enrolment confirmation; SheerID), then book flights marked student deal. Only one verified student per booking, so each friend books separately.
conditions: Not every route has a student deal; BASIC fare only; rebooking and cancellation follow the normal Eurowings rules; a Flyla service fee may apply; Eurowings and Flyla say verification matches a central database of enrolled students, and it is not stated whether Norwegian institutions are covered.
relevantForTRD: Low: Eurowings has no known Trondheim service, so it could only help on a separate intra-Europe leg (for example within Germany) and only if Flyla can verify the students.
notes: eurowings.com blocks direct fetches (403); read through search extracts restricted to eurowings.com. The discount size conflicts between Eurowings pages (50% vs 80%). The Flyla step-by-step guide describes the original Lufthansa/Eurowings seat-filling concept ('up to 70%'), which is marketing language.

appliesTo: Not applicable: Finnair's FAQ states it has no special fares for youth. Travellers aged 12 and over use normal adult tickets; a reduced child ticket exists only for accompanied children.
benefit: None found. No student fare found either.
howToBook: Not applicable (regular fares only; start a reservation on finnair.com to see prices).
conditions: Not applicable.
relevantForTRD: No youth or student fare to use; Finnair can only be booked at regular prices (the Wikipedia airport list shows a seasonal Trondheim-Helsinki route, possibly outdated).
notes: The Finnair FAQ page was fetched directly (footer shows copyright 2026) and says 'Finnair doesn't have special fares for youth.' A Finnair Norway page 'Youth Fares for 18 to 25-year-olds' (finnair.com/no/gb/nuorisohinnat) appeared in search results but now returns HTTP 404, so it is dead. A past one-off 70% youth sale on Finnish domestic routes (undated news item) does not apply.

appliesTo: Not applicable: airBaltic's pages only describe child and infant discounts (children 2-11 up to 25% off, infants 90% off) and the unaccompanied-minor service; teens from 12 may fly alone on an adult ticket.
benefit: None found for youth or students.
howToBook: Not applicable.
conditions: Not applicable.
relevantForTRD: No youth or student fare to use; airBaltic can only be booked at regular fares.
notes: Absence-based finding: searches restricted to airbaltic.com found no youth or student fare; a discount-code site (Savoo) says airBaltic has no student discount programme. Several airBaltic pages are 1.5-2 years old. One result mentioning an airBaltic youth offer was a spam page and was ignored.

ageRange: 18-25 (LOT's student fare terms: reached 18th but not 26th birthday and verified as a student by Flyla; LOT page says under 26)
appliesTo: Student fares via Flyla on domestic flights within Poland only, one-way, Economy, only on routes that have a special student fare, and only for flights departing less than 30 calendar days after booking. Other LOT flights can be booked on Flyla but at regular prices.
benefit: Cheaper domestic Poland fares for verified students; LOT page says up to 80% off the regular price on selected routes. Checked baggage is a flat paid add-on on these fares.
typicalSaving: LOT page: up to 80% off on selected domestic routes (no typical value).
howToBook: Create a Flyla account, pass student verification, and buy on flyla.com (tickets cannot be bought on lot.com); tickets cannot be bought for several passengers from one account.
conditions: Verification required; one-way domestic only; 30-day departure window; no youth fare without student verification found; LOT child discounts (25% international, 40% domestic for ages 2-12) are irrelevant here.
relevantForTRD: Marginal: it cannot help a Trondheim departure or any international sector, only a domestic Poland leg (for example Warsaw-Gdansk or Krakow) booked within 30 days of travel.
notes: lot.com blocks direct fetches (Akamai access denied); content read through search extracts restricted to lot.com, which agree on domestic-only, one-way and the 30-day window. Flyla's own FAQ is broader ('may be available on short-haul and long-haul routes') but LOT's page is the authority and says domestic Poland only.

appliesTo: Icelandair's own pages show no youth or student fare. Flyla lists Icelandair student deals on selected routes, including Europe-North America, without terms.
benefit: Nothing confirmed on icelandair.com: only a 20% fare discount for children 2-11, and Saga Club membership from age 12 (a loyalty programme, not a fare). Flyla says student fares may include checked baggage but states no discount.
howToBook: Not applicable on icelandair.com. If a student fare exists it is sold via flyla.com after student verification.
conditions: Unknown.
relevantForTRD: No usable discount on Icelandair's own site, and Flyla's mention concerns transatlantic student fares, not Trondheim-Europe or Reykjavik legs.
notes: Source conflict: Flyla (partner platform) lists Icelandair student deals while Icelandair's own pages and a coupon site show no student or youth fare. Marked null rather than false because the Flyla claim could not be confirmed or refuted on icelandair.com. Many Icelandair pages are 1-6 years old.

ageRange: Student passenger type: 12-34 (not yet 35) on international flights; 12-25 on domestic Turkish flights and flights to Ercan. The Youth Club (12-25) is for Turkish citizens only.
appliesTo: Flights operated by Turkish Airlines only (not AJet, codeshares or Star Alliance partner flights), Economy, one-way or return; covers Europe-Istanbul sectors and transit via Istanbul.
benefit: Discount on the base fare (taxes excluded): 10% on flights to or from Turkiye, 15% on international transit flights (both ends outside Turkiye), 20% domestic (Ercan 15% or 20%, pages conflict). Student tickets get a 40 kg baggage allowance on international routes and the first change is free (fare-class difference may be charged).
typicalSaving: 10% (to/from Turkiye) to 15% (transit), base fare only; up to 20% domestic.
howToBook: Join Miles&Smiles, submit the Student Application Form on turkishairlines.com (member number, name, date of birth, plus student ID, ISIC card, student certificate or transcript); Turkish says checks take about 7 business days; then log in and choose Student as the passenger type when booking.
conditions: Student status valid 1 year; the original document may be requested at check-in (copies not accepted); cannot be combined with other Turkish campaigns or the Youth Club discount; not valid for flights from EU countries to Russia; rate varies by route, class and date.
relevantForTRD: Low: Turkish Airlines does not fly from Trondheim, so it only helps for Oslo-or-other-hub to Istanbul sectors on Turkish aircraft (Trondheim-Oslo on a separate ticket) if the trip goes to or via Istanbul, and the approval takes about a week so apply early.
notes: turkishairlines.com timed out on direct fetch; terms were read through search extracts restricted to turkishairlines.com and cross-checked on the Student Beans Norway page (fetched directly, dated Oct 2026) which lists the same ages (12-34 transit, 12-25 domestic), 15% transit and 7-working-day verification. Conflicts: one Turkish fare-rules page lists a Student 12-25 category; the Ercan rate is 15% on one page and 20% on another. A press release titled 'Students, time to step on board and discover Europe' is an expired 2017 Hong Kong promotion and not relevant.

ageRange: Under 30 (until the day before the 30th birthday). One Iberia page says 16-29, the Swedish site fare page lists 12-24, so the sources conflict.
appliesTo: Iberia Joven under-30 fares on flights operated by Iberia, Iberia Express and Air Nostrum, lowest Economy fares, only when booked through the Iberia Joven site. Partner pages (ISIC, REAJ) describe it as European flights departing from Spain, which would exclude a Trondheim departure; Iberia's own notes exclude some flights (Puente Aereo, inter-island, certain concerted routes) and require return trips to start and end in the same city.
benefit: 10% off the fare (taxes and surcharges not discounted); 15% when booking for 4 or more passengers according to Iberia Joven pages. A separate Go Study fare for students on mobility programmes (Erasmus, internships abroad) adds one extra 23 kg bag and one free change on the return.
typicalSaving: 10% of the base fare (15% for 4+ passengers), taxes and surcharges not discounted.
howToBook: Register with Iberia Club (Iberia Plus on some national sites), sign up at joven.iberia.com and book from the Iberia Joven area, where the discounted fare is shown.
conditions: Age checked with ID at travel; discount only on bookings made on the Joven site; eligible destinations change with the current offer; Go Study benefits cannot be added to tickets already bought.
relevantForTRD: Low: Iberia does not serve Trondheim and the discount appears tied to flights departing from Spain, so it could only matter for a Spain-origin leg of the trip.
notes: joven.iberia.com and iberia.com block direct fetches (403); read through search extracts. Page ages vary (some 2-3 years old). The 'departing from Spain' restriction comes from partner pages, not from the main under-30 notes page, so it is unconfirmed whether a non-Spanish origin is excluded.

appliesTo: Not applicable: Vueling's help and fare pages show only a resident discount (75% for Balearic, Canary, Ceuta and Melilla residents, extra for large families), Vueling Club (Avios) and child rules; no youth or student fare was found.
benefit: None found for youth or students.
howToBook: Not applicable.
conditions: Not applicable.
relevantForTRD: No youth or student fare to use; Vueling can only be booked at regular fares.
notes: Absence-based finding from four searches (English and Spanish) restricted to vueling.com and help.vueling.com plus open searches; a 'student/senior 10%' line in a Vueling menu PDF concerns the Vueling bus service, not flights.

appliesTo: Inconclusive. TAP's fares page says it has special prices for infants and young people on some routes (indicate the category when booking) but only spells out ages 2-11; fare tables show a 'Young Adults (12-15 years)' category. No 12-25 youth fare or student fare with rules was found.
benefit: Nothing confirmed for 23-year-olds.
howToBook: Unknown; TAP says to indicate the category (student, young person) when making the reservation, if it applies on the route.
conditions: Unknown.
relevantForTRD: Unknown and probably nil: nothing confirms a youth or student fare on TAP, and TAP does not serve Trondheim.
notes: The TAP fares-and-taxes page was fetched directly twice and contains no text about special prices for young people, students or infants even though search extracts quote such a sentence, so the page content is inconsistent between access methods. English and Portuguese searches found no TAP youth or student fare. To settle it, ask TAP or run a live search on flytap.com with passenger type options.

appliesTo: ITA Airways Young offer on flights operated by ITA Airways to destinations in Italy and Europe (a newer terms version adds North Africa and the Middle East). Excludes Territorial Continuity itineraries such as Milan-Alghero. The separate Youth Flight Pass covers Italian domestic routes only.
benefit: Lower youth fare (no percentage stated; a 2025 summer promo had one-way fares from EUR 45 but has expired). Changes allowed before and after departure for a penalty (EUR 30 or EUR 65 per change, pages conflict); no refund; no free seat selection; only hand baggage is mentioned.
howToBook: On ita-airways.com via the Youth/Young offer page; the fare needs an advance purchase of at least 1 day. The exact passenger-type label in the booking engine was not visible in the extracts.
conditions: Limited seats per day and flight; ITA may check eligibility at boarding and deny boarding if age cannot be proven (the passenger may be offered to pay the difference to the adult fare); unaccompanied minors 12-14 excluded; no changes after a no-show.
relevantForTRD: Moderate for Italy-bound legs, for example Copenhagen or Amsterdam to Rome or Milan on ITA aircraft, but not for the Trondheim departure itself.
notes: ita-airways.com blocks direct fetches (403); read through search extracts restricted to ita-airways.com (several regional mirrors agree on age 12-25 and the 1-day advance purchase). Conflicts between terms versions: change penalty EUR 30 vs EUR 65 and the destination list. Checked-baggage allowance on the Young fare was not stated. No booking or travel window for the standard Young fare was found.

appliesTo: genAIRation AEGEAN youth programme: tickets on the whole Aegean (and Olympic Air) network, in Greece and abroad, booked online through the genAIRation page while logged in.
benefit: Fixed 15% discount on tickets that can stack with other offers, a one-time 50% welcome voucher for a first trip after ID upload (a March 2026 blog says it is valid 6 months), two free 23 kg checked-bag vouchers per year (pages vary), free onboard Wi-Fi, plus Miles+Bonus membership.
typicalSaving: 15% (blog says it excludes taxes and fees, so the real saving is nearer 6%); 50% one-time welcome voucher.
howToBook: Register or log in at aegeanair.com/genAIRation (or the Aegean app), upload an ID or passport to verify age, then search and book through the genAIRation page while logged in.
conditions: Age verified by ID upload; companies excluded; benefits issued as vouchers in the account; tickets only bookable online through the genAIRation page; the programme ends on the day the member turns 26.
relevantForTRD: Low to moderate: it only helps on Aegean/Olympic flights, for example if the trip includes Athens, Thessaloniki or a Greek island, and Aegean is not a Trondheim carrier except for seasonal charters.
notes: en.aegeanair.com blocks direct fetches (403); read through search extracts restricted to aegeanair domains, plus a travel-dealz article of 15 Mar 2026 (fetched, third party) that agrees on 18-25, 15% and the 50% voucher. Aegean's genAIRation terms page is about 1.5 years old and contains a date typo; baggage-voucher details differ between pages (2 free checked bags per year vs 2 vouchers of 23 kg). The 50%-off-for-a-pet voucher is irrelevant here.

appliesTo: No youth or student fare for individual travellers. The only student rate is for student groups (all passengers students under 25 on the travel date, minimum group of 11 or, in an older version, 16). WIZZ Discount Club is a paid membership that is not age-based.
benefit: None for 2-5 individual travellers. Discount Club paid tiers give about EUR 10 off fares from EUR 19.99 and EUR 5 off online checked bags.
howToBook: Not applicable for individuals.
conditions: Student groups: documents may be checked at check-in and carriage can be refused if requirements are not met.
relevantForTRD: No: a group of 2-5 friends does not qualify for the student group rate; Wizz Air has had a Trondheim presence (its airport ground-handling contract from January 2026 includes Trondheim and the Wikipedia list shows Gdansk), but only at regular fares.
notes: The Wizz group terms page returned HTTP 405 on direct fetch and was read through search extracts; the two versions disagree on minimum group size (11 vs 16). The WIZZ Youth Challenge is a student business competition, not a fare. Trondheim route facts are from third-party aviation sources and may be outdated.

appliesTo: No age-based youth fare found. The only student offer is the Erasmus offer for holders of an ESNcard (Erasmus Student Network), bookable only on the dedicated Erasmus booking platform on Ryanair.com (not the app); excludes domestic flights, connecting and third-party flights and Regular, Plus and Flexi Plus fares.
benefit: 10% off four one-way flights or two return flights plus a free 20 kg checked bag on each flight booked (Ryanair's 2025-26 announcement); Ryanair help pages in places state 15%.
typicalSaving: 10% (some Ryanair help pages say 15%) on up to four one-way or two return flights, plus a free 20 kg bag.
howToBook: Obtain an ESNcard (esncard.org), add its number to the myRyanair profile and book on the Erasmus platform on Ryanair.com, normally at least 28 days ahead; the card can be checked at the airport.
conditions: ESNcard required (boarding can be refused without it); terms mention travel periods such as 1 Sept to 15 June and a 28-day advance booking; the 2026-27 extension was not found.
relevantForTRD: None in practice: Ryanair does not appear to serve Trondheim, and ESN Trondheim issues ESNcards to international and exchange students, volunteers and buddies, telling Norwegian students going on exchange to get the card abroad.
notes: help.ryanair.com returned 403 on direct fetch; terms were read through search extracts. The corporate press release (13 Aug 2025) was fetched directly: 10% on four one-way flights or two returns and a free 20 kg bag for registered ESN students. eligibleAt23 is null because it depends on holding an ESNcard, which Norwegian degree students in Trondheim generally cannot get (ESN Trondheim page fetched directly); ESN volunteers or Erasmus-student buddies can. Ryanair has no youth (under 26) fare.

appliesTo: Not applicable: easyJet's terms treat anyone 16 or older as an adult, children 2-15 are charged the normal fare, and no youth or student fare was found.
benefit: None found. A third-party aggregator (HappyFares) claims a 10% student fare with 10 kg extra baggage, but this is unverified and not on easyJet's own pages.
howToBook: Not applicable.
conditions: Not applicable.
relevantForTRD: No youth or student fare to use; easyJet is not shown on the Trondheim airport route list.
notes: Absence-based finding: searches restricted to easyjet.com found no student or youth fare; Save the Student (third party) says easyJet does not offer a student discount (page fetch returned 403, quote taken from the search extract). The HappyFares claim conflicts and was not confirmed.

appliesTo: Luxair and Luxairtours flights, SMART and FLEX fares (extra airline outside the requested list, included because it has a youth fare).
benefit: Fixed amount off: EUR 20 off a return flight and EUR 10 off a one-way flight in SMART and FLEX, EUR 40 off a Business Class return.
typicalSaving: EUR 20 off a return, EUR 10 off a one-way (EUR 40 off Business return).
howToBook: luxair.lu flight search: select Youth as the passenger type.
conditions: Not valid on promotional tickets (W class); the offer page gives no validity dates; proof of age is not mentioned on the offer page, so carry ID.
relevantForTRD: Only relevant if the trip includes Luxembourg or a Luxair route; it is not a Trondheim carrier.
notes: The Luxair offer page was fetched directly. Luxair was not on the requested list; a search extract also said proof of age may be required.

ageRange: Youth up to 26; full-time students up to 33 (an older KILROY page gave different limits)
appliesTo: KILROY youth and student flight tickets, worldwide, including Europe: KILROY says it has its own prices on flexible youth and student tickets to Europe. The page names no airlines.
benefit: Flexibility rather than a stated discount: date changes within validity (subject to seat availability), sometimes route changes, often free stopovers; refundable for a fee. KILROY says prices are about the same as standard tickets but can be cheaper.
howToBook: flights.kilroy.no, phone +47 2310 2310 (Mon-Fri 09-17), chat, or the Oslo office. A valid ISIC digital student card (students; about 100 NOK, valid 12 months) or IYTC digital youth card is required and must be carried for the whole trip.
conditions: Date change fee 950 NOK per ticket (online terms) or an administrative fee of 750 NOK per ticket for changes or cancellations (general terms), plus the airline's own fee; refund of airport taxes costs 450 NOK; cancellation at least 24 hours before first departure; no name changes; unused part of a partly used ticket is not refunded; the ticket is only valid under the age limit at departure; the airline's terms apply to the carriage.
relevantForTRD: Worth a quote for a return flight with flexible dates, but KILROY says its prices are about the same as standard tickets and its change fees (750-950 NOK plus airline fee) reduce the benefit for a fixed 8-day trip.
notes: All KILROY pages were fetched directly. Conflicts: change fee 950 NOK (changes page) vs 750 NOK (general terms); age limits 26/33 on the current page vs an older page. No actual fare for Trondheim-Europe was obtained and the airlines used are not stated, so the value for this trip is unknown.

ageRange: 18-25 per the current BYOjet help page; older StudentUniverse pages said 16-25 or under 26
appliesTo: Student and young-adult discounted fares on participating airlines; StudentUniverse has been renamed BYOjet for Students and now sells to everyone regardless of age or student status. The BYOjet homepage lists airlines such as Air New Zealand, Cathay Pacific, Emirates, Etihad, Qantas, Singapore Airlines, Turkish Airlines and Virgin Australia; no European short-haul airline is listed. Departures from Norway are not documented.
benefit: Unlocked discounts after student verification; no percentage stated and the company says airfares are not guaranteed to be cheaper than retail.
howToBook: On the search results page choose the prompt to unlock discounts, enter passenger ages, complete student verification, then book.
conditions: Full-time student with valid ID (BYOjet help page); carry student ID or proof of age when travelling (booking terms); name must match ID; non-students can also book at normal prices.
relevantForTRD: Unlikely to help: the airline list is long-haul and US-centric and nothing shows Norwegian departures or European short-haul student fares.
notes: studentuniverse.com and home.byojet.com blocked direct fetches (403); content read through search extracts restricted to those domains. The Flyla comparison article is a competitor's text. Eligibility changed during the rebrand, so the age range conflicts between pages.

ageRange: ISIC: full-time students over 12 with no upper age limit; IYTC youth card for people 30 or younger who are not students
appliesTo: In Norway the only flight benefit found on isic.no is access to KILROY Flights (ISIC/ITIC/IYTC); ISIC's global benefits site also lists airline offers such as Emirates (long-haul) and a Turkish Airlines agent arrangement. No European short-haul airline offer for Norway was found.
benefit: Eligibility card for KILROY youth/student fares and some airline student desks; no flight discount percentage was verifiable for Norway.
howToBook: Order the card on isic.no (about 100 NOK; the page also says 10 EUR) as a digital card in the ISIC app, valid 12 months; then buy through KILROY or the airline's student scheme.
conditions: Full-time student means at least 15 hours a week for at least 12 weeks a year at a publicly approved school or university; card valid 12 months.
relevantForTRD: Only indirectly: the ISIC (or IYTC) card is the proof KILROY requires, and the card also serves as accepted student document for the Turkish Airlines student programme.
notes: isic.no pages were fetched directly. The home page says 'Spar pa flybilletter med ditt ISIC-, ITIC- eller IYTC-kort' under KILROY Flights; badges such as 'Opptil 35 EUR rabatt' and '30 % ISIC-rabatt' are not clearly tied to flights, so no percentage is claimed. The Norwegian ISIC pages state two prices (100 NOK and 10 EUR).

appliesTo: Student deals on partner airlines through flyla.com; partner lists on Flyla pages and press name Eurowings, Lufthansa Group, ITA Airways, Norwegian, SAS, Turkish Airlines, Icelandair, LOT, Widerøe, Loganair and Etihad (varies by source). Deals exist only on selected routes and flights and Flyla's deal pages for Norwegian, SAS and Widerøe state no terms.
benefit: Student-only seats on some flights; marketing claims up to 50-80% off on some routes; no concrete discount for a Trondheim-Europe trip could be verified.
howToBook: Register on flyla.com, verify enrolment (upload enrolment confirmation; SheerID partnership), then book flights marked student deal. One verified student per booking; a Flyla service fee may be charged.
conditions: Only students verified on Flyla can book student deals; non-students and unverified users get standard fares; deals are per person; availability depends on route, date and inventory; contract is with the airline and the fare rules of the airline apply.
relevantForTRD: Possibly useful for a quick last-minute check of SAS, Norwegian, Eurowings or ITA student deals, but each friend must verify and book separately and it is unconfirmed that Norwegian enrolment can be verified.
notes: Flyla pages were fetched directly and are mostly templated marketing text; they state no age limit, no countries, and no discount amounts. The munich-startup article (29 Feb 2024) names LOT, Widerøe and Loganair as newest partners; the full partner list comes from a search extract and Flyla's home page. Flyla's own FAQ and blog are the only sources for verification, so treat claims as unconfirmed until a live Flyla search shows prices.

provider: Norwegian student unions and welfare bodies (SiT, NTNU, Studentersamfundet, NSO)
appliesTo: No airline or flight discount deal was found through SiT (Trondheim student welfare organisation), NTNU, Studentersamfundet i Trondhjem (Samfundet) or the national student organisation NSO. The student travel discounts that did surface in Norway are for trains and local transport (for example Vy student discount for students under 30, Ruter 30-day pass).
benefit: None found for flights.
howToBook: Not applicable.
conditions: Not applicable. The ESNcard from ESN Trondheim (300 NOK) gives the Ryanair Erasmus offer but is for international students, exchange students, volunteers and buddies, not for Norwegian degree students.
relevantForTRD: Nothing found that helps with flights; the student ID from NTNU/SiT mainly serves as proof of status for airline student schemes such as Turkish Airlines or Flyla.
notes: Absence-based: four Norwegian and English searches on SiT, NTNU, Samfundet and NSO found no travel-agency or flight arrangement; members' benefit pages (samfundet.no, sit.no) were not read directly. Marked null rather than false because a member-only benefit could exist behind a login. The Vy rail detail comes from a search extract.

appliesTo: UNiDAYS Norway lists a travel category but no airline was visible without logging in; Student Beans Norway lists Turkish Airlines student offers that repeat Turkish Airlines' own programme (Student passenger type, Miles&Smiles, ages 12-34 for transit flights).
benefit: No airline discount specific to these platforms was verified.
howToBook: Not applicable; use the Turkish Airlines student application described in that entry.
conditions: Membership requires verifying student status (UNiDAYS: re-verify every 12 months).
relevantForTRD: No verified airline offer for a Trondheim-Europe trip.
notes: The UNiDAYS brand list is behind login and was not readable; the Student Beans Turkish Airlines page was fetched directly (dated Oct 2026) and matches Turkish Airlines' own terms.
